sections.title: Player text
sections.body: The brush goes still. Whatever you did, it is done. The horses breathe hard. The road smells like wet thorn, churned mud, and adrenaline fading too slowly. Among what was dropped, you see gear that does not look like bandit scrap: stamped buckles, route tags, and filed-off inventory marks from the same kind of system that hired you.

Caption: After the fight, the module asks what victory cost and what the party learned.
Mood: Cargo Reclaimers
Gmgoal: Turn the outcome of the ambush into consequence, truth, and the next route toward the village.
Publicobjective: Decide what to do with what just happened and get the package moving again.

Readaloud: The brush goes still. Whatever you did, it is done. The horses breathe hard. The road smells like wet thorn, churned mud, and adrenaline fading too slowly. Among what was dropped, you see gear that does not look like bandit scrap: stamped buckles, route tags, and filed-off inventory marks from the same kind of system that hired you.
Gmnotes: Mercy route: leader or survivors talk. Combat route: gear and effects talk. Either route should leave the party asking who benefits from a dangerous forest.

Gmscript: Say: "The fight is over. The outcome matters now." If mercy or negotiation opened trust, say: "Up close, these people look less like bandits and more like former workers who have been sleeping rough and losing for a long time." If the party killed or routed them, say: "The gear tells the story the survivors cannot: company issue, filed off and reused." If players ask for the truth, use Presence or Knowledge 14, or mercy already earned, to reveal: "They were company or preserve workers who say the danger reports were manufactured to sell protection and discard the people who noticed."

Gmreadaloud: The brush goes still. Whatever you did, it is done. Among what was dropped, you see gear that does not look like bandit scrap: stamped buckles, route tags, and filed-off inventory marks. The road smells like wet thorn, churned mud, and adrenaline fading too slowly.

Gmchecklist: Read bramble_outcome before choosing variant tone. Set bramble_truth_learned only if mercy/parley, survivor dialogue, or Presence/Knowledge 14 earns it. Unlock location maps only for spared, negotiated, captured-with-care, or escaped-with-contact routes. Give a thread, not the whole campaign explanation.

Gmprivate: The workers' claim is the first load-bearing truth thread, but the driver-killer canon flag remains unresolved. Do not mention Keystone Asset in player-facing aftermath. If players pursue the communities, use the two location maps as optional discovery, not mandatory plot.
Playertakeaway: You do not have the whole picture, but you have seen enough to question who benefits from a dangerous forest.
Storytakeaway: The attackers were tied to the same company world that hired the party; the forest's danger story no longer matches the evidence.
Mechanictakeaway: The mechanic here is consequence: bramble_outcome and bramble_truth_learned decide what doors open next.

Playerquestions: What detail in After the Ambush tells you the official story is incomplete? Who notices the human cost first, and how do they show it? What small object, smell, or sound makes this scene feel real?
Relationshipprompts: Which PC quietly checks on someone else here? Who disagrees about the right thing to do without breaking trust?
Ownershipprompt: Name one detail in After the Ambush that belongs to your character's point of view.

Fearspends: Spend Fear to reveal omitted risk, split attention, or put a human cost in front of the contract. Close the ambush net or put a PC between cargo and a frightened reclaimer. Reveal a personal effect that makes victory emotionally complicated.

Choicesconsequences: Question survivors with care Presence 14 or earned mercy reveals the worker-displacement thread. Location maps can open and Act 3 starts with sharper questions. Threat interrogation may get facts but close trust. Search dropped gear Knowledge 14 reads company issue and filed inventory marks. Truth is thinner without survivors but still points at the company story cracking. Ignoring gear leaves bramble_truth_learned false. Tend the wounded or bury the dead Mercy becomes visible to any survivor. A guide, safe route, or future ally can become available. Looting first makes later trust harder.

Lootclues: Personal effects Route sketch Old Goldspire seal Bramble Union Stoneweave: A garment of thousands of tiny polished stones moves like cloth and turns thorns like armor. Every fitted piece looks cut by hands that loved the work. Vial of Briarpowder: A small stoppered vial holds fine grey-green thorn powder that seems to drink the light. A blade edge near it looks sharper and hungrier. Bramble Ward-Scrap Charm Cluster: A knot of blue ward shards, twine, and tiny salvage tags clacks softly at a Bramblefolk belt. It looks illegal only because it looks useful.

Storyscope: Perceived antagonist: the forest. True antagonist: the corporate lie about the forest. The players never confront it directly. They are meant to feel it by the end. Every act offers at least one guaranteed and one earned hint that the danger is manufactured and the forest is not the enemy. The reclaimers target the cargo and manifest, not purses, and avoid killing when possible. REFLAVOR GUARANTEED Their gear includes salvaged, repainted Grail/Kazrak kit: ex-workers, not feral bandits.
